content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multi-region failover started automatically from us-east-1 -> eu-central-1. Telemetry shows ~18% of sessions still affinity to us-east-1 and an uptick in 502/503 responses. Investigate.
harper: on pager, joining. pulling health and routing state now.
nate: I see Route53 weighted records were flipped but BGP session to one upstream peer in us-east-1 still advertising the /18. Possibly route leak from partner.
lin: checking LB states and target health. Several targets in us-east-1 report healthy but NAT gateway is showing high connection counts.
ops-liaison: pinged peering partner NOC to confirm they withdrew routes. Awaiting reply.
harper: runbook: follow multi-region failover steps. Step 1: verify DNS weights — route53 list-rrsets shows weight eu=100 us=0 but real traffic still hitting us-east front door.
nate: dumping BGP table on our edge:
```
# bgp-summary --peer all
peer-10.x.y.z (partner) : prefixes 1.2.0.0/18 advertised (localpref 200)
```
nate: partner still advertising old prefix via their transit. Asking them to withdraw.
lin: in parallel, we can edge-redirect via CDN origin failover so clients hitting us-east edge get proxied to eu-central origin.
harper: create CDN rule to origin-fallback to eu-central for host header *.api.redwood
lin: pushing CDN change now.
deploy-bot: CDN config deploy started (deploy-8921)...
deploy-bot: CDN config deploy finished :white_check_mark: (deploy-8921)
lin: CDN change applied. Synthetic traffic from multiple vantage points shows 95% requests served from eu-central now, but some TCP sessions already established to us-east are still alive and erroring.
ops-liaison: partner NOC replied: they had an automation misfire during maintenance and briefly re-advertised the prefix; they've now started withdrawal, estimate 6-8 minutes to converge.
harper: mitigation: evict stuck connections on problematic LB nodes and reduce deregistration_delay to 5s to accelerate drain.
lin: running commands on LB pool:
```
# reduce deregistration
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=5
# force close conntrack entries on hosts still showing many established sockets
ssh node-1234 'sudo conntrack -D --orig-dst 10.20.30.40/32'
```
harper: executed conntrack flush on 4 hosts. Observed immediate drop in established sockets.
nate: traceroutes from failing client IPs now show AS path ending at our transit not partner. Looks like partner withdraw worked partially.
cs-manager: CS impact: 7 customers showing elevated error rates (>10%) for API endpoints used by webhooks. Two customers reported duplicate webhook deliveries due to retries. Drafting customer note now.
ops-liaison: note — we saw some iptables conntrack timeouts unusually high; adding kernel param tuning to runbook as action item.
harper: monitoring: overall 5xx reduced from 18%->2% over last 10 minutes after conntrack flush + CDN failover, still a few edge nodes with sporadic 502s.
lin: found one proxy instance in us-east in crashloop during failover window — it caused some 502s. Restarted container and isolated bad config.
deploy-bot: service restart executed on proxy group (restart-3004) :white_check_mark:
harper: after restart and conntrack flush, error rate baseline restored. Need to leave mitigations in place until BGP fully converges and partner confirms full withdraw.
nate: partner confirms withdraw completed at 3161712800 UTC — BGP tables show eu path only.
lin: CDN fallback still active, keeping for 30m buffer. I'll schedule rollback after postmortem actions applied.
cs-manager: outbound update sent to affected customers: short blameless summary + mitigation steps + ETA for full confirmation. Customers acknowledged and asked for postmortem.
harper: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0424 and assigning to platform for postmortem. Immediate action items recorded: 1) add partner maintenance checklist to avoid accidental re-advertisements, 2) add automated conntrack reduction during failovers, 3) CDN fallback smoke tests in CI, 4) instrument BGP withdraw detect and auto-notify.
ops-liaison: noted we also need to record kernel tuning changes and ensure they are safe across fleets.
harper: handoff reminder — next oncall (nate) in 18m. I will stay on for 10m to monitor then handoff.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0424 created by harper at 3161712345. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/multi-region-failover
nate: compiling logs and commands to incident doc. Will include partner comms timestamps and BGP dumps.
lin: adding action item to reduce default DNS TTLs for planned failovers; also note edge caches can exceed TTLs in practice.
cs-manager: final update to customers will include timeline, mitigation, and credits if SLA breached. Keeping CS loop open.
harper: monitoring holds steady for 22m, error rate at baseline. If stable for 30m, we'll mark resolved.
nate: postmortem owners assigned: harper/lin/nate. Will draft and circulate within 48 hours.
cs-manager: thanks team. Closing customer comms after postmortem review.
harper: thanks all. Good coordination. :clap:
